Agent Model

Bayesian agent models.

The abstract AgentModel encapsulates both the agent’s beliefs and the thought processes that an ideal Bayesian agent would use in the context of decision support. The agent has priors, can make a decision based on those, can update his beliefs when presented with new information in the form of an observation and a prediction for it, and can make decisions based on his posterior beliefs.

MultivariateAgentModel is the multivariate concrete implementation: the covariate vector X is k-dimensional, the predictive model is an OLS regression of Y on X (with or without intercept), and the agent observes a single observed feature vector X_o together with the scalar prediction pred_o produced for it.

Instead of representing the historical plate of training patients explicitly, the model uses the low-dimensional sufficient-statistic reduction of the plate. The observed prediction has an exact conditional Normal distribution given the reduced covariate statistics, so the OLS outcome-noise projection is integrated analytically.

ScalarAgentModel is the scalar concrete implementation, where the regression coefficients are fixed constants rather than learned parameters.

class agent_model.AgentModel(plate_size, prior_parameters=None, predictive_var_names=None)[source]

Bases: ABC

This abstract class serves as blueprint for all agent models. The hardcoded assumptions are:

  1. you have two treatment options A1_treatment and A0_treatment,

  2. you are interested in one outcome Y,

  3. all features are encoded in X.

The class requires you to define your model and sampling method. That is, you have to define your beliefs about the data generating process (both prior distributions and SCM), and you have to define how you believe the model and prediction were generated from unseen data. The last step is necessary to generate posterior samples and should preferably be computationally efficient (plate reduction!).

classmethod load_agent_model(file_name='agent_model', folder='./saved_models/')[source]

Load a saved agent model.

The configuration is loaded with joblib and the PyMC model is reconstructed by re-running __init__. The trace and prior samples are loaded from their NetCDF files if present.

Parameters:

  • file_name (str) – Base filename without extension. Expects to find {file_name}.joblib and, optionally, {file_name}_trace.nc and {file_name}_prior_samples.nc.

  • folder (str) – Folder the model is saved in.

Returns:

The loaded agent model.

Return type:

MultivariateAgentModel

posterior_parameter_summaries()[source]

Compute mean, std, skewness, and kurtosis of the posterior samples for each population parameter (the variables sampled in trace.posterior).

For scalar parameters (N_E, alpha_mu_A, …) returns one set of moments per parameter. For vector parameters (alpha_mu_X, N_b, …) with k = 1 returns one set without a dimension index; with k > 1 returns one set per dimension.

Returns:

Summary statistics keyed by param_<name>_<moment> (scalar or k = 1) or param_<name>_<dim>_<moment> (k > 1).

Return type:

dict

sample_posterior_predictive_summaries(rng=None)[source]

Method that estimates the mean, standard deviation, skewness, and kurtosis of the variables X, A, and Y in the posterior predictive samples.

For k = 1, X is summarized as a scalar (post_X_<moment>), matching A and Y. For k > 1, X is k-dimensional and is summarized per covariate dimension instead (post_X_<dim>_<moment>).

Returns:

Summary statistics keyed by post_<var>_<moment> (A, Y, and X when k = 1) or post_X_<dim>_<moment> (X when k > 1).

Return type:

dict

save_agent_model(file_name='agent_model', folder='./saved_models/')[source]

Save the agent model configuration and available samples.

The trace and prior samples are written separately with ArviZ (NetCDF), and the rest of the configuration is pickled with joblib. The PyMC model, trace, and prior samples are temporarily detached before pickling and restored afterwards.

Parameters:

  • file_name (str) – Base filename without extension. Creates {file_name}.joblib and, when available, {file_name}_trace.nc and {file_name}_prior_samples.nc.

  • folder (str) – Folder to save the model into.

trace_diagnostics()[source]

Return basic sampler diagnostics for the current posterior trace.

A component that is exactly constant is omitted because its R-hat and ESS are undefined but it has no Monte Carlo error. Any other undefined diagnostic raises an error instead of being skipped by xarray.

Returns:

max_rhat, min_ess_bulk, min_ess_tail (computed with ArviZ), and n_divergences.

Return type:

dict

class agent_model.AgentModelNormalPredictions(n_covariates, plate_size, prior_parameters=None, predictive_var_names=None, fit_intercept=True)[source]

Bases: MultivariateAgentModel

This class implements an Agent Model based on the finding that the Prediction pred^o follows a normal distribution given X. This is because all remaining transformations are then linear and as the error term follows a normal distribution, also the predictions is normally distributed.

class agent_model.MultivariateAgentModel(n_covariates, plate_size, prior_parameters=None, predictive_var_names=None, fit_intercept=True)[source]

Bases: AgentModel

Class for a multivariate agent model with structural equations:

\(Y_i = N_b^\top X_i + N_{E} A_i + N_{Yi}\)

\(A_i = N_d^\top X_i + N_{Ai}\)

\(X_i = N_{Xi}\)

where N_{Xi}, N_{Ai}, N_{Yi} are normal noise variables drawn for every instantiation of the plate, N_{E} is a normal variable drawn once per instantiation of the plate, and the coefficient vectors N_b and N_d are likewise drawn once per instantiation. The structural intercept is carried by alpha_mu_Y.

Rather than modeling the plate of plate_size patients explicitly, the model reduces it to the covariate sufficient statistics (s, W). Conditional on these variables, the observed prediction has an exact Normal distribution obtained by integrating the OLS outcome-noise projection.

Parameters:

  • n_covariates (int) – Number of covariates k (dimension of X).

  • plate_size (int) – Size of the plate (number of i.i.d. samples used to train the predictive model). Must be larger than n_covariates.

  • prior_parameters (dict) – Dictionary with parameters for the prior distributions. If None, defaults are used. Vector-valued entries accept a scalar (broadcast to length k) or an array of length k.

  • predictive_var_names (list) – Names of the variables sampled for predictive calculations. If None, defaults are used.

  • fit_intercept (bool) – Whether the predictive model is an OLS with an intercept. Both variants use the reduced covariate statistics (s, W).

Returns:

None

class agent_model.ScalarAgentModel(plate_size, prior_parameters=None, scm_constants=None, predictive_var_names=None)[source]

Bases: AgentModel

Class for a scalar agent model with structural equations:

\(Y_i = a + b X_i + N_{E} A_i + N_{Yi}\)

\(A_i = d X_i + N_{Ai}\)

\(X_i = N_{Xi}\)

where N_{Xi}, N_{Ai}, N_{Yi} are normal noise variables drawn for every instantiation of the plate and N_{E} is a normal variable drawn once per instantiation of the plate. Unlike MultivariateAgentModel, the regression coefficients a, b, and d are fixed constants, not learned parameters with their own priors.

Rather than modeling the plate of plate_size patients explicitly, the model reduces it to three auxiliary variables: s (the sum of covariate noises), W (the centered covariate dispersion), and g (the outcome-noise projection). From these, the OLS slope coefficient phi of the external predictive model (a no-intercept regression of Y on X) is reconstructed analytically.

Parameters:

  • plate_size (int) – Size of the plate (number of i.i.d. samples used to train the predictive model).

  • prior_parameters (dict) – Dictionary with parameters for the prior distributions. If None, defaults are used.

  • scm_constants (dict) – Dictionary with the fixed structural coefficients a, b, and d. If None, defaults are used.

  • predictive_var_names (list) – Names of the variables sampled for predictive calculations. If None, defaults are used.

Returns:

None
